title: A mortar shell took his leg in Kargil. He taught himself to run on a blade instead. October 8, 2026.
excerpt: From an air force that started with 5 pilots, to a navy ship built to keep others at sea longer, to a soldier who ran marathons after losing a leg in war, October 8's five stories are about capacity built the hard way - institutional, financial and personal.
bodyHtml:
Every story today is about extending capacity that didn't exist before - an air force that grew from five pilots into a national institution, a navy that can now stay deployed longer, a seed business whose proceeds became a rural development foundation, a sarod lineage that found a global audience through collaboration, and a soldier who rebuilt his own physical capacity after losing a leg in war.

October 8, 1932: India's air force began with 5 pilots and 4 biplanes

The Indian Air Force Act, 1932 came into force, establishing the force with five Cranwell-trained pilots and four Westland Wapiti biplanes based at Karachi. It took its current name in 1950 and October 8 has been observed as Air Force Day ever since.

A sarod maestro and his two sons recorded an album with the Dalai Lama. It won a Grammy

Ustad Amjad Ali Khan, with sons Amaan and Ayaan Ali Bangash, won the 68th Grammy Award for Best Audio Book, Narration and Storytelling Recording for 'Meditations: The Reflections of His Holiness the Dalai Lama' - pairing the Dalai Lama's spoken reflections with three generations of sarod artistry.

His uncle built India's hybrid seed industry, then sold it all to fund rural development

Dr. Suri Sehgal built Proagro Group and Hytech Seed India before selling them in 1998 and founding the S M Sehgal Foundation in 1999. His nephew Jay Sehgal became Chairperson in April 2025, carrying the work across more than 3,000 villages in 13 states.

India just launched a ship whose only job is keeping other warships at sea longer

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh launched 'Surya,' India's first indigenous Fleet Support Ship, at Hindustan Shipyard on October 6, 2026 - part of a Rs 19,000 crore, 5-ship program letting India's navy resupply at sea instead of returning to port.

A mortar shell landed 1.5 metres from him in the Kargil War. Gangrene took his leg. He taught himself to run on a blade instead

Major D.P. Singh lost his leg to a war injury during the 1999 Kargil War. In 2011 he became the first Indian to complete a marathon on a blade prosthesis, later running at high altitude near Leh and becoming the first Indian amputee to skydive solo in 2019.

Five stories, one thread: an air force built from five pilots, a navy extending its reach at sea, a family's business proceeds turned into rural infrastructure, a musical lineage that found its audience by collaborating outward, and a soldier who rebuilt his own capacity to run. Nothing here started at scale - all of it got there.
